title: 第三节论空间和时间观念的其他性质

content.value:
上面所提及的那个发现（即：印象总是发生于观念之先，同时由想象提供的每一个观念都首先出现于与之相应的印象中），对于解决关于观念的所有争论而言，没有什么比这个发现更令人感到愉快的了。这些较后的知觉都是如此的清楚和明显，以至它们不容有争论；不过我们的许多观念却是相当的嗨涩，即使是形成它们的心灵也几乎不可能去断定它们的本质和构成。为了进一步发现我们的空间和时间观念的本质，我们可以应用这一原理。
当我张开眼睛并环视四周的对象时，我就感知到许多可见的物体；而当我又将眼晴闭上并思考这些物体之间的距离时，我就获取了广延的观念。正像每个观念都是来自于与之精确地相似的某个印象一样，和这个广延的观念类似的印象也必然要么是来自于视觉的一些感觉，要么是由这些感觉产生的某种内在印象。
我们的内在印象是我们的情感、情绪、欲望和厌恶，我相信，
这些印象中的任何一个都不会被看作是产生空间观念的范本。
这样，剩下的就只有感官能将这个原始的印象传送给我们。那么，我们的感官在这里能传送什么印象给我们呢？这是一个首要的问题，它无须诉求就决定着观念的本质。

The table before me is alone sufficient by its view to give the idea
of extension. This idea, then, is borrow’ d from, and represents some
impression, which this moment appears to the senses. But my senses
convey to me only the impressions of colour′ d points, dispos′ d in a
certain manner. If the eye is sensible of any thing farther, I desire it
may be pointed out to me. But if it be impossible to shew any thing
farther, we may conclude with certainty, that the idea of extension is
nothing but a copy of these colour′ d points, and of the manner of
their appearance.
Suppose that in the extended object, or composition of colour′d
points, from which we first receiv' d the idea of extension, the points
were of a purple colour; it follows, that in every repetition of that idea
we wou’ d not only place the points in the same order with respect to
each other, but also bestow on them that precise colour, with which
alone we are acquainted. But afterwards having experience of the other
colours of violet, green, red, white, black, and of all the diferent
compositions of these , and finding a resemblance in the disposition of
colour′ d points, of which they are compos′ d, we omit the peculiari-
ties of colour, as far as possible, and found an abstract idea merely
on that disposition of points, or manner of appearance, in which they
agree. Nay even when the resemblance is carry'd beyond the objects
of one sense, and the impressions of touch are found to be similar to
those of sight in the disposition of their parts; this does not hinder the
abstract idea from representing both, upon account of their resem-
blance. All abstract ideas are really nothing but particular ones, con-
sider' d in a certain light; but being annexed to general terms, they
are able to represent a vast variety, and to comprehend objects,
which, as they are alike in some particulars, are in others vastly wide
of each other.
The idea of time, being deriv' d from the succesion of our per-
ceptions of every kind, ideas as well as impressions, and impres-
sions of reflection as well as of sensation, will afford us an instance
of an abstract idea, which comprehends a still greater variety than

在我眼前的这张桌子，单是看它一眼就足以给予我关于广延的观念。因此；这个观念就是由此刻出现于感官前的某一印象而来，并表象这个印象的。但是，我的感官传送给我的仅仅是以某一方式排列的色点的印象，如果说眼睛还能进一步感觉到任何东西，我希望有人能把这个东西指给我。但是如果不可能再指出任何东西，我们就可以确定地断言，广延的观念仅仅是这些色点和它们的皇现方式的一个摹本。
假设在我们最先获取广延观念的那个占有空间的对象或色点的构成中，这些点是紫色的；那么，随之而来的就是，那个观念在每一次重复出现时，我们不仅要把这些点各自放人相同的次序内，而且还要把那种仅仅是为我们所熟悉的确切颜色安放到那些点上。但是，后来我们文经验到紫罗兰色、绿色、红色、白色、黑色等其他颜色，并且经验到了所有这些颜色的不同构成，同时发现了组成这些颜色的色点的排列也有类似性，这样我们就尽可能地忽略颜色的特性，仅仅是根据色点相同的排列方式和呈现方式去形成一个抽象观念。不仅如此，即使是在这种类似性被推进到某一感官对象之外，并且触觉印象和视觉印象在其各个部分的排列方面也被发现有类似之处时，也不能阻碍这个抽象观念依据它们的类似性去同时形成关于二者的表象。所有的抽象观念实际上都仅仅是依据某一确定的视角而加以考察的特殊观念；但是，由于这些抽象观念附着于一些一般名词之上，所以它们就能够表象大量的各种不同观念，并且包含了一些虽然在某些细节方面类似，但在其他更多的方面互相之间却存在巨大差距的对象。
同空间观念相比，还有一种抽象观念，它虽然包含了数量更为巨大的各种不同的观念，但仍然为某个有确定数量和性质的特

that of space, and yet is represented in the fancy by some particular
individual idea of a determinate quantity and quality.
As’ tis from the disposition of visible and tangible objects we re-
ceive theideaof space，sofrom the sucessionofideas and mpres
sions we form the idea of time, nor is it possible for time alone ever to
make its appearance, or be taken notice of by the mind. A man in a
sound sleep, or strongly occupy’d with one thought, is insensible of
time; and according as his perceptions succeed each other with grea-
ter or less rapidity, the same duration appears longer or shorter to his
imagination. It has been remark ' d by a great philosopher, that our
perceptions have certain bounds in this particular, which are fix′ d by
the original nature and constitution of the mind, and beyond which no
influence of extermal objects on the senses is ever able to hasten or re-
tard our thought. If you wheel about a burming coal with rapidity, it
will present to the senses an image of a circle of fire; nor will there
seem to be any interval of time betwixt its revolutions; meetly be-
cause’tis impossible for our perceptions to succeed each other with the
same rapidity, that motion may be communicated to extermal objects.
Wherever we have no successive perceptions， we have no notion of
time, even tho’there be a real succession in the objects. From these
phaenomena, as well as from many others, we may conclude, that time
cannot make its appearance to the mind, either alone, or attended with
a steady unchangeable object, but is always discover' d by some per-
ceivable succession of changeable objects.
To confirm this we may add the following argument, which to me
seems perfectly decisive and convincing. 'Tis evident, that time or du-
ration consists of different parts : For otherwise we cou’d not conceive
①Mr.Locke.

殊的个体观念在想象中所表象。时间观念就为我们提供了这种抽象观念的一个实例，它来自于我们各种知觉的相互接续中，这些知觉既包括观念也包括印象，既包括反省印象也包括感觉印象。
正像我们是从可视的和可触知的对象的排列中获取空间观念一样，我们是从观念和印象的相互接续中形成时间观念的，时间永远不可能单独地呈现自身，也不可能单独地为心灵所注意。
一个正在醋睡或署冥思苦想的人是难以感觉到时间的，而根据他的各种知觉的互相接续或快或慢，同一持续的时间在他的想象中就会显得或长或短。一位伟大的哲学家曾经谈到，我们的知觉在这一方面有某种界限，这种界限由心灵的原始本质和构造所决定，如果我们超出了这种界限，外在对象对感官的影响就永远不能使我们的思想得到加速或延缓。如果你快速地旋转一块正在燃烧着的煤，将会有一个火环的意象呈现于感官，并且看起来在每次旋转的中间也不会有任何时间的间隔；这仅仅是因为我们不可能使知觉的互相接续同传给外在对象的那种运动有着相同的速度。只要我们没有接续的知觉，我们就没有时间概念，即使在对象中存在着一个真正的接续。我们可以根据这些和许多其他的现象推断出，时间既不可能单独地，也不可能伴随着一个稳定而不可改变的对象呈现于心灵中，它总是由可变对象的某种能够知觉的接续才得以发现的。
为了证实这一点，我们可以加上下面这个在我看来有着十足决定性和说服力的论证。显然，时间或者持续是由不同的
①洛克先生。

a longer or shorter duration. ' Tis also evident, that these parts are not
co-existent: For that quality of the co-existence of parts belongs to ex-
tension, and is what distinguishes it from duration. Now as time is
compos’ d of parts, that are not co-existent; an unchangeable object,
since it produces none but co-existent impressions， produces none
that can give us the idea of time; and consequently that idea must be
deriv'd from a succession of changeable objects, and time in its first
appearance can never be sever' d from such a succession.
Having therefore found, that time in its first appearance to the
mind is always conjoin’ d with a succession of changeable objects,
and that otherwise it can never fall under our notice, we must now ex-
amine whether it can be conceiu′ d without our conceiving any suces-
sion of objects, and whether it can alone form a distinct idea in the i-
magination.
In order to know whether any objects, which are join' d in im-
pression, be separable in idea, we need only consider, if they be
different from each other; in which ease,' tis plain they may be
conceiv′ d apart. Every thing, that is different, is distinguishable;
and every thing, that is distinguishable, may be separated, ac-
cording to the maxims above-explain’ d. If on the contrary they be
not different, they are not distinguishable; and if they be not dis-
tinguishable, they cannot be separated. But this is precisely the
case with respect to time, compar’ d with our successive percep-
tions. The idea of time is not deriv′ d from a particular impression
mix′ d up with others, and plainly distinguishable from them; but
arises altogether from the manner, in which impressions appear to
the mind, without making one of the number. Five notes play′ d on
a flute give us the impression and idea of time; tho′ time be not a
sixth impression, which presents itself to the hearing or any other
of the senses. Nor is it a sixth impression, which the mind by re-
flection finds in itself. These five sounds making their appearance in
this particular manner, excite no emotion in the mind, nor produce an

部分组成的，因为如果不是这样的话，我们就不能设想-一个或长或短的持续时间。同样显然的是，这些部分不是共存的，因为各个部分共存的性质属于广延，而且这也是广延和持续能够加以区分的地方。既然时间是由不共存的各个部分组成，而又由于一个不变的对象只能产生共存的印象，因此它就不能产生出给予我们时间观念的任何印象；因此，观念必定是源自于各种可变对象的接续，而且时间在其最初呈现时也绝不能和这样的接续分开。
因此，我们就已经发现了，在最初呈现于心灵时，时间总是和可变对象的接续联结着的，否则它就绝不会被我们注意到。现在，我们必须考察，如果我们没有设想任何对象的接续，我们能否设想出时间的存在，以及它能否单独地在想象中形成一个清晰的观念。
为了知道在印象中结合若的任何对象是否可以在观念中分离，我们仅仅需要去考察这些对象彼此间是否存在差异；如果存在差异，则它们显然是可以分别被设想的。根据上述公理，凡是存在差异的事物都是可以区分的，而凡是可以区分的事物都是可以分离的。相反，如果它们不存在差异，它们就不能加以区分；如果它们不能被区分，它们就不能被分离。但是，同我们接续的知觉相比，时间正好是这种情形。时间观念并不是源自于一个混合于其他印象中，并可以明显地和这些印象相区分的特殊印象；而是完全来自于各种印象皇现于心灵的方式、而它却不能成为这些印象中的一个。在笛子上演奏出的五个音符给予我们时间的印象和观念，但是时间并不是呈现于听觉或其他任何感官的第六个印象，同时也不是心灵在反省自身时发现的第六个印象。当这五种音以这种特殊的方式出现时，既不会在心中激起任何的情绪，也不
—73一

affection of any kind, which being observ′ d by it can give rise to a
new idea. For that is necessary to produce a new idea of reflection,
nor can the mind, by revolving over a thousand times all its ideas of
sensation, ever extract from them any new original idea, unless nature
has so fram’ d its faculties, that it feels some new original impression
arise from such a contemplation. But here it only takes notice of the
manner, in which the different sounds make their appearance; and
that it may afterwards consider without considering these particular
sounds, but may conjoin it with any other objects. The ideas of some
objects it certainly must have, nor is it possible for it without these i-
deas ever to arrive at any conception of time; which since it appears
not as any primary distinct impression, can plainly be nothing but dif-
ferent ideas, or impressions, or objects dispos′ d in a certain manner,
that is, succeeding each other.
I know there are some who pretend, that the idea of duration is
applicable in a proper sense to objects, which are perfectly unchange-
able ; and this I take to be the common opinion of philosophers as well
as of the vulgar. But to be convine′ d of its falsehood we need but re-
flect on the foregoing conclusion, that the idea of duration is always
deriv'′ d from a succession of changeable objects, and can never be
convey' d to the mind by any thing stedfast and unchangeable. For it
inevitably follows from thence, that since the idea of duration cannot
be deriv′ d from such an object, it can never in any propriety or ex-
actness be apply′ d to it, nor can any thing unchangeable be ever said
to have duration. Ideas always represent the objects or impressions,
from which they are deriv′ d, and can never without a fiction repre-
sent or be apply'd to any other. By what fiction we apply the idea of
time, even to what is unchangeable, and suppose, as is common,
that duration is a measure of rest as well as of motion, we shall con-
sider Wafterwards.

会产生在其被观察时能产生一个新的观念的任何感情。因为对产生一个新的反省观念而言，那种情形是必需的。即使心灵对它所有的感觉观念重复思考一千次，它也不能从中得到任何新的原始观念，除非自然已经设计了心灵的能力，使它感到通过这样一种沉思会产生一些新的原始印象。但是，在这里，心灵仅仅是注意到了不同的声音出现的方式：这就使得我们在随后可以不去考虑这些特殊的声音，而仅仅去考虑这种方式，而且可以把这种方式同其他的任何对象结合起来。
的确，心灵必须要有一些对象的观念，如果没有这些观念，它就永远不可能获得任何时间的概念；既然这个概念不是作为任何原始的清楚的印象出现，显然它就只能是以某种排列方式，也即相互接续的方式出现的不同的观念、印象或对象。
我知道，一些人会认为，持续的观念在适当的意义上应用于完全不可改变的对象；在我看来，这不仅是普通人，而且也是哲学家们所持有的一般观点。但是我们只要回顾一些前面的结论就能确信这一观点的谬误，这个结论就是，持续观念总是源自于可变对象的接续，它永远不能被笃定的和不可改变的任何事物传入心中。因为由此就不可避免地得出，既然持续的观念不是源自于这样的一个对象，它就绝不能在任何适当或精确的意义上应用于这样一个对象，也不能将任何不变的东西说成是持续的。观念永远表象着产生它们的对象或印象，而且没有虚构就绝不能表象或应用于其他的任何对象。究竞是什么样的虚构能使我们把时间观念甚至应用于不可改变的对象，并且如通常所设想的，持续不但是运动的衡量标准，而且也是静止的衡量标准，我们将在以后加以考察。①

There is another very decisive argument, which establishes the
present doctrine concerming our ideas of space and time, and is foun-
ded only on that simple principle, that our ideas of them are compoun-
ded of parts, which are indivisible.This argument may be worth the ex-
amining.
Every idea, that is distinguishable, being also separable, let us
take one of those simple indivisible ideas, of which the compound one
of extension is form′ d, and separating it from all others, and consid-
ering it apart, let us form a judgment of its nature and qualities.
'Tis plain it is not the idea of extension. For the idea of exten-
sion consists of parts; and this idea, according to the supposition, is
perfectly simple and indivisible. Is it therefore nothing? That is abso-
lutely impossible. For as the compound idea of extension, which is re-
al, is compos′ d of such ideas;were these so many non-entities, there
wou′d be a real existence compos′ d of non-entities; which is ab-
surd. Here therefore I must ask, What is our idea of a simple and indi-
visible point? No wonder if my answer appear somewhat new, since
the question itself has scarce ever yet been thought of. We are wont to
dispute concerning the nature of mathematical points, but seldom con-
cerming the nature of their ideas.
The idea of space is convey' d to the mind by two senses,
the sight and touch; nor does any thing ever appear extended,
that is not either visible or tangible. That compound impression,
which represents extension, consists of several lesser impressions,
that are indivisible to the eye or feeling, and may be call′ d impres-
sions of atoms or corpuscles endow' d with colour and solidity.
But this is not all.′ Tis not only requisite,that these atoms
shou’d be colour′ d or tangible， in order to discover themselves
to our senses; ′ tis also necessary we shou' d preserve the idea of
their colour or tangibility in order to comprehend them by our imag-
ination. There is nothing but the idea of their colour or tangibility ,
一76一

还有另一个非常有决定性的论证，它建立了我们目前关于空间和时间观念的学说，而且它仅仅是建立在“我们的时间和空间观念都是不可分割的许多部分的复合”这个简单原理上。这个论证也许值得加以考察。
凡是可以区分的观念也都是可以分离的，我们可以任取其中一个形成复合的广延观念的简单而不可分割的观念，把它同所有其他的观念分开，并对它进行单独考察，以对它的本质和性质形成一个判断。
显然，这个观念不是广延观念。因为广延观念是由许多部分组成的；同时，根据假定，这个观念是绝对简单和不可分割的。它会因此是一种不存在的东西吗？那完全是不可能的。因为真正的复合广延观念是由这样的一些观念组成，如果这些观念都是一些非实体，那将会有一个由一些非实体组成的真实存在，这种说法是荒谬的。因为我在这里必须要问：我们简单而不可分的点的观念是什么呢？如果我的答案显得有些新奇那也毫不奇怪，因为这个问题本身几乎从未被思考过。我们习惯于对数学点的本性进行论争，但却很少争论它们观念的本性。
空间的观念是通过视觉和触觉这两个感官传入心灵中的，任何不可见或不可触知的事物永远都不会看起来有广延。表象广延的那个复合印象是由几个较小的印象组成的，对于视觉和触觉来说，这些较小的印象是不可分割的，它们可以被称作赋有颜色和坚固性的原子或粒子的印象。但这并不是全部。不仅要求这些原子必须是有颜色的或可触知的，以使它们呈现自身于我们的感官，而且我们还必须保存它们的颜色或可触知的观念，以使它们为我们的想象所包含。只有它们的颜色或可触知的观念才能使这些
—77一

which can render them conceivable by the mind. Upon the removal of
the ideas of these sensible qualities, they are utterly annihilated to the
thought or imagination.
Now such as the parts are, such is the whole. If a point be not
consider' d as colour′ d or tangible, it can convey to us no idea; and
consequently the idea of extension, which is compos′d of the ideas of
these points, can never possibly exist. But if the idea of extension re-
ally can exist, as we are conscious it does, its parts must also exist;
and in order to that, must be consider’ d as colour’ d or tangible. We
have therefore no idea of space or extension, but when we regard it as
an object either of our sight or feeling.
The same reasoning will prove, that the indivisible moments of
time must be fill' d with some real object or existence, whose succes-
sion forms the duration, and makes it be conceivable by the mind.
SECTION IV.Objections Answer'd.
Our system concerming space and time consists of two parts,
which are intimately connected together. The first depends on this
chain of reasoning. The capacity of the mind is not infinite; conse-
quently no idea of extension or duration consists of an infinite number
of parts or inferior ideas, but of a finite number, and these simple
and indivisible:’ Tis therefore possible for space and time to exist
conformable to this idea: And if it be possible,'tis certain they actu-
ally do exist conformable to it; since their infinite divisibility is utterly
impossible and contradictory.
The other part of our system is a consequence of this. The parts,
into which the ideas of space and time resolve themselves, become at
last indivisible; and these indivisible parts , being nothing in themselves ,
are inconceivable when not fill′ d with something real and existent.

原子为心灵所想象。一旦除去这些可感知性质的观念，它们对思想或想象来说就完全被消灭了。
既然部分是如此，整体也会是如此。如果一个点不被认为是有颜色或可触知的，它就不能传送给我们任何观念；因此这些点的观念组成的广延观念就绝不可能存在。但是，如果广延观念如我们所意识到的那样能真正地存在，那么它的部分也必定会存在；而要存在，就必须被看作是有颜色或可触知的。因此，除非我们把空间或广延的观念看作是我们视觉或触觉的对象，否则我们就没有这样的观念。
相同的推理可以证明，时间的不可分的瞬间必定充满着某种真实的对象或存在物，这种对象的接续形成了持续，并使它能为心灵所设想。
